items.title: Mercury 3 Preview on ARC-AGI (verified): 61.8% ARC-AGI-2 at $0.06 per task, first diffusion model evaluated, up to 1,743 tokens per second
items.summary: ARC Prize published verified results for Inception's Mercury 3 Preview: 88.5% on ARC-AGI-1 and 61.8% on ARC-AGI-2 at a few cents per task, with throughput near 1,000 output tokens per second. Builders get a reproducible look at what a diffusion language model does on reasoning tasks.

items.title: LoRA adapter makes Qwen3.8-27B a stronger agent behind the Pi harness: SWE-Bench Pro Hard subset 29% to 63%, 55-62% fewer tool calls
items.summary: A released LoRA adapter tunes Qwen3.8-27B to the Pi coding harness, reporting 29% to 63% on a 51-task SWE-Bench Pro Hard subset and 40% to 56% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, using far fewer tool calls. More harness-specific adapters are promised.

doubt.pushback: Gains are on a small 51-task subset and self-reported; not independently reproduced yet.

items.title: GLM-5.3-Flash on two DGX Sparks: switching vLLM to TensorFold lifts 4-stream throughput from 54.6 to 85.2 tok/s, split into engine, draft model and dense-layer quantization
items.summary: A home-lab test on the same two DGX Sparks and same scripts compared five configurations, with each stream given a different prompt, and attributes the speedup to three separate pieces. Full report and raw data are on GitHub.

items.title: Hugging Face's 1,000-agent swarm on ELIZA-2026: agents spent most time waiting on merges and context, only 40-60 of 1,000 calling the model at once
items.summary: Hugging Face describes scaling a swarm of over 1,000 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash agents on a couple of B200 nodes to build PyBot, finding the bottlenecks in git merges, tests and context re-reading rather than GPUs (about 130 tokens read per token written). Swarm tooling (flock, msgboard) is promised in the coming days.

doubt.pushback: Tooling and detailed results not yet released, so the numbers cannot be checked.

items.title: BAAI PhysCapBench: 1,500-sequence benchmark of how well video captions preserve real-world physics, with physical captions cutting world-model error
items.summary: BAAI introduced a benchmark scoring video captions on seven physical dimensions across third-person and egocentric scenes, and reports that physics-grounded captions reduce reconstruction error in world models and improve robot policy success on RoboTwin 2.0. BAAI says everything is open-sourced.

doubt.pushback: Primary repo or paper link could not be confirmed from the post text.

items.title: Ant Group's Inclusion AI introduces Duo, a reciprocal world model for real-time audio-video interaction, ~708 ms end-to-end latency
items.summary: Inclusion AI presents Duo v1, which models an agent's intent and its audiovisual realization together. On 30 real-time duplex interactions (180 checks) it reports 100% on language, speech and identity, 96.7% emotion consistency, 73.3% content responsiveness and about 708 ms latency, with an arXiv paper.

doubt.pushback: Small self-run evaluation; arXiv link not confirmed from post text.

items.title: Ling 3.0 Flash Sante on two DGX Sparks: medical QA reproduces model-card numbers on two of three benchmarks (MedQA 94.6%, MedMCQA 82.4%), MedXpertQA falls short at 45.0%
items.summary: A one-week local test ran 500 questions per benchmark at the same settings and compared to the model card: two benchmarks matched, the hardest one landed about 5 points below the card.

items.title: SenseTime releases sensenova-loop-9b weights on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0
items.summary: A tracker account reports SenseTime's 9B sensenova-loop model is now open-weight with an Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face.

doubt.pushback: Secondhand report; Hugging Face link not confirmed in this pass.

items.title: Self-Improving Memory: model discovers its own memory skills and trains them into its weights
items.summary: A new method meta-optimizes memory skills from the model's own runs, then distills the gains into the weights; the post links a blog and a six-part thread.

doubt.pushback: No numbers visible in the opening post.

items.title: Agent toolkit for training an object detector for about $6: keypoint and OCR models as agent tools plus an end-to-end detection trainer
items.summary: Merve packaged her favorite vision models as tools for an agent to call, plus a trainer that goes from labeling through VLM-as-judge to training and eval, and added decision-model support and newer VLMs. A talk and GitHub repo accompany it.

doubt.pushback: Repository link is in a follow-up post and was not checked.

items.title: tiny-voca text-to-speech ported to an ESP32-S3, generating audio faster than real time
items.summary: Xuan-Son Nguyen ran the 4.5M-parameter tiny-voca TTS fully on a microcontroller, with most delay coming from phonemization.

items.title: TensorFold on a Mac Studio M5 Ultra generates MiniMax-Image in 12.6 s versus 80.6 s on a DGX Spark, whose port is new
items.summary: A head-to-head comparison attributes the gap to a tuned Mac build that keeps the model loaded versus a brand-new Spark port that spends half its time on setup; a rematch is promised.
